cards.name: IVGMetadata
cards.summary: The document-properties record of a CorelDRAW document (Document.Metadata): title, subject, author, keywords, notes, copyright, revision and language, plus the template fields (type, industry, sidedness, folds, designer notes) the template browser reads. It changes no artwork; it is what File > Document Properties shows and what is saved inside the .cdr.
use_for: stamp title, author, copyright and keywords on every file a batch job saves (client deliverables, archive search)
tag a .cdr saved as a template with its type, industry, sidedness and folds so it sorts properly in the template browser
read the author / last author / revision of incoming files in an audit or file-intake script
avoid: metadata inside an exported PDF: the PDF export settings (PDFSettings) carry their own Author / Subject / Keywords (there is no Title setting there); set those on the export, do not rely on these being copied (unverified)
any visual change: nothing here touches the page; use the shape and page classes
cards.how: One per document, reached as ActiveDocument.Metadata (IVGDocument.Metadata). Plain string properties (Title, Subject, Author, Keywords, Notes, Copyright, Template*) are read and written directly; the Localizable* properties and Category return IVGLocalizableString objects that hold one string per language (SetLangString / GetLangString / DefaultLangString). Changes live in the open document and reach disk only when the document is saved.

key_members.name: Title
key_members.use: document title (string)

key_members.name: Subject
key_members.use: document subject (string)

key_members.name: Author
key_members.use: creator name (string)

key_members.name: LastAuthor
key_members.use: who edited the file last; described as 'returns', so treat it as informational even though it is not flagged read-only

key_members.name: Keywords
key_members.use: keyword string used by search / template browser

key_members.name: Notes
key_members.use: free-text notes

key_members.name: Copyright
key_members.use: copyright line

key_members.name: Revision
key_members.use: revision number (long)

key_members.name: DocLanguage
key_members.use: cdrTextLanguage the document is designed for, e.g. cdrLanguageNone (0), cdrArabic (1025)

key_members.name: DocID
key_members.use: unique ID string of the document contents

key_members.name: TemplateType
key_members.use: template type text (banner, poster ...)

key_members.name: TemplateIndustry
key_members.use: template target industry text

key_members.name: TemplateSided
key_members.use: template sidedness text (single or double)

key_members.name: TemplateFolds
key_members.use: number of folds, stored as a string

key_members.name: TemplateDesignerNotes
key_members.use: designer notes shown for a template

key_members.name: LocalizableTitle
key_members.use: per-language title (IVGLocalizableString)

key_members.name: LocalizableKeywords
key_members.use: per-language keywords (IVGLocalizableString)

key_members.name: Category
key_members.use: document category; only available as an IVGLocalizableString

gotchas: setting a property only changes the open document: call ActiveDocument.Save (or SaveAs) or the values are lost on close
the Localizable* properties and Category are read-only object references: you cannot assign a string to them, call SetLangString / DefaultLangString on the returned IVGLocalizableString instead
IVGLocalizableString.SetLangString takes the language as a string, not a cdrTextLanguage value; the expected code format is not in the harvest (unverified: probe GetLanguages on a file first)
TemplateFolds and TemplateSided are strings, not numbers or enums; use the exact wording the template dialog writes (unverified)
writing metadata probably marks the document modified (Dirty = True), which triggers a save prompt on close in an interactive session (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim md As Metadata
Set md = ActiveDocument.Metadata
md.Title = "Diwali sale poster A3"
md.Author = "Studio"
md.Keywords = "diwali; poster; A3"
md.Copyright = "(c) 2026 Studio"
ActiveDocument.Save

review.changes: avoid: PDF export settings have Author / Subject / Keywords, not Title (checked IPDFVBASettings in the harvest)

cards.name: IVGNode
cards.summary: One node (anchor point) of a CorelDRAW curve: its position, node type (cusp / smooth / symmetrical), its place in the subpath and the node-level edits the Shape tool offers on it: move, delete, break apart, join, connect, extend, average, and the fillet / chamfer / scallop corner treatments.
use_for: round, bevel or scoop a single corner of a logo or badge outline (Fillet / Chamfer / Scallop)
move or snap one anchor point to an exact coordinate in a generated shape
close a gap between two open path ends (JoinWith / ConnectWith / ExtendSubPaths) after a trace or import
read node positions to measure or rebuild a path in another tool
avoid: editing many nodes at once: get an IVGNodeRange (Curve.Nodes.All or Nodes.Range) and call its batch methods instead of looping node by node
shapes that are still rectangles, ellipses, polygons or text: they have no editable nodes until ConvertToCurves (or use the shape's own corner-radius properties for rounded rectangles)
cards.how: Not created directly. Reach it from a curve shape: Shape.Curve.Nodes(i) (1-based), Curve.Nodes.First / Last, SubPath.StartNode / EndNode, Curve.FindNodeAtPoint(x, y), or from another node with Next / Previous. A node belongs to one curve (Parent) and one subpath (SubPath); positions are page coordinates in the document's unit (ActiveDocument.Unit).

key_members.name: PositionX
key_members.use: X of the node on the page, read / write, document units

key_members.name: PositionY
key_members.use: Y of the node on the page, read / write, document units

key_members.name: SetPosition
key_members.use: set X and Y in one call

key_members.name: Move
key_members.use: shift by DeltaX, DeltaY (both optional, default 0)

key_members.name: Type
key_members.use: cdrNodeType: cdrCuspNode 0, cdrSmoothNode 1, cdrSymmetricalNode 2

key_members.name: Index
key_members.use: position inside its subpath (presumably 1-based like Nodes(i), unverified)

key_members.name: AbsoluteIndex
key_members.use: position inside the whole curve

key_members.name: IsEnding
key_members.use: True for the first or last node of its subpath (harvest wording; whether a closed subpath reports it is unverified)

key_members.name: Next
key_members.use: method: the following node

key_members.name: Previous
key_members.use: method: the preceding node

key_members.name: Segment
key_members.use: the segment that ends at this node

key_members.name: NextSegment
key_members.use: the segment that leaves this node

key_members.name: Delete
key_members.use: remove the node; the path re-forms through its neighbours

key_members.name: BreakApart
key_members.use: split the path at this node into two unconnected end nodes

key_members.name: JoinWith
key_members.use: join this end node with another end node into one node

key_members.name: ConnectWith
key_members.use: connect this node to another one if possible (closes the gap with a segment, unverified)

key_members.name: ExtendSubPaths
key_members.use: extend two open subpaths until they meet; JoinPaths optional (default False)

key_members.name: AveragePositionWith
key_members.use: move this node and Node2 to their midpoint; JoinPaths optional

key_members.name: Fillet
key_members.use: round a cusp corner with Radius; returns True on success

key_members.name: Chamfer
key_members.use: bevel a corner with DistanceA / DistanceB; returns bool

key_members.name: Scallop
key_members.use: cut an inward round notch with Radius; returns bool

gotchas: node collections are 1-based and the numbering changes after Delete, BreakApart, Fillet, Chamfer or Scallop (one node becomes two): re-fetch nodes or walk the indices from the end, never keep stale Index values

Fillet / Chamfer / Scallop return a bool; expect False rather than an error when the node cannot take it (an end node, a smooth node, or a radius too big for the adjacent segments) and check the result (unverified)
the shape must be a curve: s.Curve on an unconverted rectangle, ellipse or artistic text gives no editable nodes; call s.ConvertToCurves first
positions follow ActiveDocument.Unit; set the unit at the start of the script or the numbers are in the user's last unit
GetPosition and GetPoint return through ByRef arguments; from Python win32com the values come back as the return tuple instead (unverified)
setting Type to smooth or symmetrical on a node between straight line segments may have no visible effect until the segments are curves (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim s As Shape, n As Node
ActiveDocument.Unit = cdrMillimeter
Set s = ActiveShape
s.ConvertToCurves
Set n = s.Curve.Nodes(1)
n.Move 5, 0
If Not n.IsEnding Then n.Fillet 3

review.changes: IsEnding reworded to the harvest ('first or last of its subpath', not 'open subpath'); Index 1-based and the Fillet/Chamfer/Scallop False-on-failure gotcha marked unverified

cards.name: IVGNodeRange
cards.summary: A working set of nodes from one curve that you edit together, like a Shape-tool node selection: move, stretch, rotate or skew them as a group, change their type, smooth or auto-reduce them, break or delete them, and fillet / chamfer / scallop all their corners in one call.
use_for: round every corner of a converted logo or icon outline at once (Nodes.All then Fillet)
clean a traced or imported path by reducing redundant nodes (AutoReduce) or smoothing jagged ones (Smoothen)
move, rotate or skew just part of a shape (a subset of nodes) without touching the rest
drive or read the user's current node selection (Curve.Selection, CreateSelection)
avoid: transforming whole objects: use the shape's own Move / Rotate / Stretch / Skew, which work on any shape type without converting it to curves
nodes from different shapes: a range belongs to one curve (Parent); work shape by shape
cards.how: Get one from a curve: Curve.Nodes.All, Nodes.Range(Array(1, 3, 5)), Nodes.AllExcluding(Array(...)), Curve.Selection (the selected nodes), a segment range's NodeRange, or start empty with Application.CreateNodeRange and fill it with Add / AddRange. Then call the batch methods; read-only PositionX / PositionY / SizeWidth / SizeHeight / BoundingBox describe the extent of the nodes.

key_members.name: Count
key_members.use: number of nodes in the range

key_members.name: Item
key_members.use: node by 1-based index

key_members.name: Add
key_members.use: add one node

key_members.name: AddRange
key_members.use: add all nodes of another range

key_members.name: Remove
key_members.use: drop a node from the range by index (does not delete it from the curve)

key_members.name: Delete
key_members.use: delete all the nodes in the range from the curve

key_members.name: Move
key_members.use: shift by DeltaX, DeltaY; optional AnchorIndex (1) and ElasticMode (False)

key_members.name: Stretch
key_members.use: scale by RatioX / RatioY (single, default 1.0), optionally about StretchAnchorX/Y

key_members.name: Rotate
key_members.use: rotate by Angle, optionally about RotationCenterX/Y when UseCenterPoint is True

key_members.name: Skew
key_members.use: skew by AngleX / AngleY, optionally about SkewAnchorX/Y

key_members.name: SetType
key_members.use: set every node to a cdrNodeType (cusp 0, smooth 1, symmetrical 2)

key_members.name: Type
key_members.use: read-only common node type, cdrMixedNodes (3) when they differ

key_members.name: Smoothen
key_members.use: smooth the curve at these nodes by a long Smoothness amount

key_members.name: AutoReduce
key_members.use: remove / edit nodes within PrecisionMargin to simplify the curve

key_members.name: BreakApart
key_members.use: break the curve at every node in the range

key_members.name: Fillet
key_members.use: round all corners in the range with Radius

key_members.name: Chamfer
key_members.use: bevel all corners with DistanceA / DistanceB

key_members.name: Scallop
key_members.use: scallop all corners with Radius

key_members.name: CreateSelection
key_members.use: make these nodes the Shape-tool node selection

key_members.name: BoundingBox
key_members.use: IVGRect around the nodes

gotchas: Range / AllExcluding take a Variant array of 1-based indices: Array(1, 3) in VBA; from Python pass a list or tuple (unverified)
on the range Fillet / Chamfer / Scallop return nothing (void), unlike the IVGNode versions which return a bool; corners that cannot take the treatment are skipped silently (unverified)
after Delete, BreakApart or a corner treatment the curve's node numbering changes; build a fresh range from Curve.Nodes before the next edit
Rotate, Skew and Stretch default to not using the anchor arguments (UseCenterPoint / UseAnchorPoint False); pass True plus the coordinates to pivot around a specific point
Smoothness and PrecisionMargin ranges are not in the harvest: probe a small value first (PrecisionMargin is presumably in document units, unverified)
Remove takes an index into the range, not a node object; RemoveRange takes another range
cards.example:
Dim s As Shape, nr As NodeRange
ActiveDocument.Unit = cdrMillimeter
Set s = ActiveShape
s.ConvertToCurves
Set nr = s.Curve.Nodes.All
nr.SetType cdrCuspNode
nr.Fillet 2
s.Curve.Nodes.Range(Array(1, 2)).Move 0, 5

review.changes: avoid: dropped the unsupported 'keep effects and fills intact' reason; shape transforms named for working without ConvertToCurves

cards.name: IVGNodes
cards.summary: The read-only collection of all nodes of a curve or of one subpath: count them, get one by 1-based index, iterate them with For Each, and turn all or some of them into an IVGNodeRange for batch edits.
use_for: walk every anchor point of a path to read or export its coordinates
pick the nodes to edit (All, Range, AllExcluding) before a batch fillet, smooth or move
count nodes to judge how heavy a traced or imported path is
avoid: adding nodes: the collection has no Add; use SubPath.AddNodeAt or Segment.AddNodeAt
deleting while iterating with For Each: collect the nodes into a range first, or loop indices from Count down to 1
cards.how: Reached as Shape.Curve.Nodes (every node of the curve) or Curve.SubPaths(i).Nodes (one subpath). Item is the default member, so Nodes(1) works; First and Last are shortcuts; All / Range / AllExcluding return IVGNodeRange objects.

key_members.name: Count
key_members.use: number of nodes

key_members.name: Item
key_members.use: node by 1-based index (default member)

key_members.name: First
key_members.use: first node

key_members.name: Last
key_members.use: last node

key_members.name: All
key_members.use: IVGNodeRange with every node

key_members.name: Range
key_members.use: IVGNodeRange with the nodes at the given indices (Variant array)

key_members.name: AllExcluding
key_members.use: IVGNodeRange with every node except the given indices

key_members.name: _NewEnum
key_members.use: enables For Each n In ...Nodes

key_members.name: Parent
key_members.use: the IVGCurve the nodes belong to (also for a subpath's collection)

gotchas: 1-based (Item is 'in base 1'): Nodes(0) is out of range and presumably raises an error (unverified)
the collection is live: Count and the index of every later node change after a node is added, deleted, broken apart or filleted
Parent is typed IVGCurve even when the collection came from a subpath; use Node.SubPath to get the subpath
Range and AllExcluding need a Variant array (Array(1, 4) in VBA), not separate arguments
cards.example:
Dim n As Node
ActiveDocument.Unit = cdrMillimeter
For Each n In ActiveShape.Curve.Nodes
  Debug.Print n.AbsoluteIndex, n.PositionX, n.PositionY, n.Type
Next n
Debug.Print ActiveShape.Curve.Nodes.Count

review.changes: gotcha: Nodes(0) raising an index error marked unverified

cards.name: IVGObjectSnapPoint
cards.summary: The object-specific part of a snap point whose type is cdrSnapPointObject: a single read-only Type that says which of the shape's object snap points it is (top, bottom, left or right). Exactly where the shape places these points is not in the harvest; they are presumably the side points connectors attach to (unverified).
use_for: pick the top / bottom / left / right attachment point of a box before drawing a connector between two boxes in a scripted flow chart or org chart
identify which object point an existing connector end is glued to
avoid: corner or centre points: those are bounding-box snap points (Shape.SnapPoints.BBox with a cdrReferencePoint)

a point part-way along an edge or at a custom spot: use SnapPoints.Edge(SegmentIndex, SegmentOffset), SnapPoints.FindClosest or SnapPoints.AddUserSnapPoint (there is no node snap-point type in cdrPointType)
cards.how: Not created directly. Get a snap point with Shape.SnapPoints.Object(cdrObjectPointTop) (or Bottom / Left / Right), then its .Object property returns this interface; for a generic IVGSnapPoint check SnapPoint.Type = cdrSnapPointObject (2) before reading .Object.

key_members.name: Type
key_members.use: cdrObjectSnapPointType: cdrObjectPointTop 1, cdrObjectPointBottom 2, cdrObjectPointLeft 3, cdrObjectPointRight 4

gotchas: the only member is Type; position, movement and deletion live on the parent IVGSnapPoint (PositionX / PositionY / IsMovable ...)
SnapPoint.Object is only meaningful when SnapPoint.Type is cdrSnapPointObject; on other snap point types expect Nothing or an error (unverified)
not every shape type may expose all four object points; check that SnapPoints.Object(...) returned something before using it (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim a As SnapPoint, b As SnapPoint
Set a = ActivePage.Shapes(1).SnapPoints.Object(cdrObjectPointBottom)
Set b = ActivePage.Shapes(2).SnapPoints.Object(cdrObjectPointTop)
Debug.Print a.Object.Type, b.Object.Type
ActiveLayer.CreateConnector a, b

review.changes: avoid: replaced non-existent 'node snap points' with SnapPoints.Edge / FindClosest / AddUserSnapPoint

cards.name: IVGOLE
cards.summary: The OLE side of a shape that holds an embedded or linked Windows OLE object (an Excel sheet, a Word table, a chart): it reports the server program, class, link path and state, opens the object for editing in place or in its own window, runs OLE verbs, and refreshes a linked object from its source file.
use_for: audit a file before print: list every OLE object, its ProgID and whether it is linked, embedded or static
refresh linked spreadsheets or charts (IsLinkUpToDate / UpdateLink) before exporting a price list or report
find links pointing at missing or moved files (LinkPath)
avoid: print or PDF artwork: an OLE object presumably renders from its cached picture and depends on the server app (unverified); paste or import the content as vectors (PDF, EMF, or native text and tables) instead
unattended scripts: Edit, Open, Activate and DoVerb start the server app's UI and can block
cards.how: Reached as Shape.OLE on a shape whose Shape.Type is cdrOLEObjectShape (12). Read the properties to learn what the object is; call UpdateLink for linked objects; Edit / Open / Activate / DoVerb hand the object to its server application.

key_members.name: Type
key_members.use: cdrOLEType: cdrOLEUnknown 0, cdrOLELinked 1, cdrOLEEmbedded 2, cdrOLEStatic 3

key_members.name: ProgID
key_members.use: program ID of the object's class, e.g. a spreadsheet or document type

key_members.name: ClassID
key_members.use: class ID (CLSID) string

key_members.name: ServerName
key_members.use: name of the application that serves the object

key_members.name: FullName
key_members.use: full object name

key_members.name: ShortName
key_members.use: short object name

key_members.name: LinkPath
key_members.use: file path of a linked object

key_members.name: IsLinkUpToDate
key_members.use: False when the linked source changed since the last update

key_members.name: UpdateLink
key_members.use: refresh a linked object from its source

key_members.name: Modified
key_members.use: True if the object was modified

key_members.name: Edit
key_members.use: edit the object in place (starts the server)

key_members.name: Open
key_members.use: edit the object in a separate server window

key_members.name: Activate
key_members.use: run the default double-click action

key_members.name: Deactivate
key_members.use: finish in-place / open editing

key_members.name: DoVerb
key_members.use: run an object-specific verb by VerbID (long)

key_members.name: IsInPlaceActive
key_members.use: True while being edited in place

key_members.name: IsOpen
key_members.use: True while being edited in a separate window

key_members.name: IsServerRunning
key_members.use: True if the server application is running

gotchas: Shape.OLE only makes sense when Shape.Type = cdrOLEObjectShape; check the type first, other shapes give Nothing or an error (unverified)
ActivePage.Shapes does not look inside groups; use ActivePage.Shapes.FindShapes(Type:=cdrOLEObjectShape) to find nested OLE objects
Edit, Open, Activate and DoVerb launch the server application and may show its window or a dialog; never call them in a headless batch, and pair Edit / Open with Deactivate
UpdateLink needs the source file at LinkPath and the server application installed; on a machine without it the call fails or keeps the stale picture (unverified)

DoVerb takes a bare long and the harvest lists no verb values; they are presumably the Windows OLEIVERB_* codes plus object-specific ones (unverified), so prefer Activate / Open / Edit, which need no ID
IsLinkUpToDate and LinkPath only apply to linked objects (Type = cdrOLELinked)
cards.example:
Dim s As Shape
For Each s In ActivePage.Shapes.FindShapes(Type:=cdrOLEObjectShape)
  Debug.Print s.OLE.ProgID, s.OLE.Type
  If s.OLE.Type = cdrOLELinked Then
    Debug.Print s.OLE.LinkPath
    If Not s.OLE.IsLinkUpToDate Then s.OLE.UpdateLink
  End If
Next s

review.changes: removed OLE verb numbers that are not in the batch (0/-1/-2/-3); cached-picture claim marked unverified; example reads LinkPath only for linked objects, matching its own gotcha

cards.name: IVGOnScreenCurve
cards.summary: A temporary XOR-drawn outline (line, rectangle, circle, point list or any IVGCurve) that a macro shows on top of the drawing window as visual feedback, the rubber-band preview a custom tool draws while dragging. It is not a shape: it is not in the document, not undoable, not printed or exported.
use_for: live preview of the outline a custom VBA / add-in tool is about to create while the user drags
highlight a region or a path on screen during an interactive macro without adding objects to the file
avoid: anything that must end up in the artwork or an export: create real shapes (ActiveLayer.CreateRectangle, CreateCurve ...) instead
headless or batch runs: nobody sees it, and it adds nothing to the document
cards.how: Created with Application.CreateOnScreenCurve, usually inside a custom tool's mouse handlers. Set the geometry with SetLine / SetRectangle / SetCircle / SetPoints / SetCurve, set the look with SetPen / SetNoPen and SetBrush / SetNoBrush, then Show; call Hide when done.

key_members.name: SetLine
key_members.use: geometry: a line from x1,y1 to x2,y2

key_members.name: SetRectangle
key_members.use: geometry: rectangle with corners x1,y1 and x2,y2

key_members.name: SetCircle
key_members.use: geometry: circle from CenterX, CenterY, Radius

key_members.name: SetPoints
key_members.use: geometry: polyline through an IVGPointRange

key_members.name: SetCurve
key_members.use: geometry: any IVGCurve (e.g. a copy of a shape's curve)

key_members.name: SetPen
key_members.use: outline: Color (long), WidthInPixels, Style (cdrOnScreenCurvePenStyle: solid 0, dash 1, dot 2, dash-dot 3, dash-dot-dot 4, alternating dots 5)

key_members.name: SetNoPen
key_members.use: draw no outline

key_members.name: SetBrush
key_members.use: fill with a Color (long)

key_members.name: SetNoBrush
key_members.use: no fill

key_members.name: Show
key_members.use: draw it on screen

key_members.name: Hide
key_members.use: remove it from the screen

gotchas: it is XOR-drawn: the colour you set mixes with whatever is under it, so the on-screen colour is not exactly the one requested (unverified)
Color is a bare long; it is presumably a Windows COLORREF as returned by VBA's RGB() (red in the low byte), not a CorelDRAW Color object (unverified)
pen width is in screen pixels while the geometry is in document coordinates (unverified for the units of the coordinates)
Hide it (and release the object) before the macro or tool ends, or the outline can stay on screen until the window redraws (unverified)
nothing it draws is part of the document, so a render or export of the page will never show it
cards.example:
Dim oc As OnScreenCurve
Set oc = Application.CreateOnScreenCurve
oc.SetPen RGB(255, 0, 0), 2, cdrOnScreenCurvePenDash
oc.SetNoBrush
oc.SetRectangle 0, 0, 100, 50
oc.Show
' ... user feedback here ...
oc.Hide

cards.name: IVGOnScreenHandle
cards.summary: A temporary XOR-drawn control handle a macro or custom tool places on the drawing window, with hit-testing (IsOnHandle) and hover highlighting (UpdateHotTracking / IsHotTracked) so the user can grab and drag it. Like the other on-screen objects it is screen feedback only, never part of the document.
use_for: draggable control points for a custom tool (e.g. the radius or angle handle of a scripted shape generator)
show a marker at a computed position (a centre, an anchor) during an interactive macro
avoid: markers that must be printed or exported: create a real shape
batch scripts with no user at the screen
cards.how: Created with Application.CreateOnScreenHandle. Place it with SetPosition(x, y), colour it with SetHandleColor, Show it; in the tool's mouse-move handler call UpdateHotTracking(MouseX, MouseY) and test IsOnHandle(MouseX, MouseY) to decide whether a press grabs it; Hide when done.

key_members.name: SetPosition
key_members.use: put the handle at x, y

key_members.name: SetHandleColor
key_members.use: handle colour as a long

key_members.name: Show
key_members.use: draw the handle

key_members.name: Hide
key_members.use: remove the handle

key_members.name: UpdateHotTracking
key_members.use: update the hover highlight from the mouse position

key_members.name: IsHotTracked
key_members.use: read-only: the handle is currently highlighted

key_members.name: IsOnHandle
key_members.use: parameterised property: True if MouseX, MouseY falls on the handle

gotchas: IsOnHandle is a property that takes arguments (MouseX, MouseY); some late-bound callers (Python win32com) need it read as a method call or through the property getter (unverified)
mouse coordinates must be in the same space as SetPosition; tool callbacks hand document coordinates, so do not pass raw screen pixels (unverified)
the handle has no drag behaviour of its own: the tool must move it with SetPosition on every mouse move
Color is a bare long, presumably a VBA RGB() COLORREF, and XOR drawing alters the shown colour (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim h As OnScreenHandle
Set h = Application.CreateOnScreenHandle
h.SetHandleColor RGB(0, 120, 255)
h.SetPosition 50, 50
h.Show
h.UpdateHotTracking 50.5, 50.5
If h.IsOnHandle(50.5, 50.5) Then Debug.Print "grabbed"
h.Hide

cards.name: IVGOnScreenText
cards.summary: A temporary XOR-drawn text label a macro or custom tool shows on the drawing window, such as a live readout of a size, angle or distance next to the cursor; it can be aligned left / right / centre, anchored by fractional xRef / yRef, and nudged by a pixel offset. Screen feedback only, never part of the document.
use_for: live measurement or angle readout beside the cursor in a custom drawing tool
short on-canvas hints during an interactive macro ("click the second point")
avoid: text that belongs in the artwork: create artistic or paragraph text shapes (ActiveLayer.CreateArtisticText)
long messages: use a form or the status bar; this is a one-line overlay
cards.how: Created with Application.CreateOnScreenText. SetTextAndPosition sets text, position and optional alignment (cdrOnScreenTextAlign: cdrLeftOnScreenText 0, cdrRightOnScreenText 1, cdrCenterOnScreenText 2) with xRef / yRef anchors (default 0.5, 0.5); SetText and UpdatePosition change one part later; SetPixelOffset keeps it a fixed number of pixels off the point; Show / Hide.

key_members.name: SetTextAndPosition
key_members.use: Text, x, y plus optional align (default 0), xRef (0.5), yRef (0.5)

key_members.name: SetText
key_members.use: change only the text

key_members.name: UpdatePosition
key_members.use: move it to x, y (e.g. on every mouse move)

key_members.name: SetPixelOffset
key_members.use: offset from the position in screen pixels (long x, y), keeps it clear of the cursor

key_members.name: SetTextColor
key_members.use: text colour as a long

key_members.name: Show
key_members.use: draw the text

key_members.name: Hide
key_members.use: remove the text

gotchas: SetPixelOffset is in screen pixels while x, y are drawing coordinates; the offset stays the same size at every zoom (unverified for the coordinate space)
xRef / yRef are presumably the fraction of the text box placed on the point (0.5, 0.5 = centred on it) (unverified)
XOR drawing: the label can be hard to read over busy artwork and its colour shifts with the background (unverified)
call Hide before the tool or macro ends, or the label can linger until the window redraws (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim t As OnScreenText
Set t = Application.CreateOnScreenText
t.SetTextColor RGB(0, 0, 0)
t.SetTextAndPosition "W 120 mm", 100, 100, cdrLeftOnScreenText, 0, 0.5
t.SetPixelOffset 12, 0
t.Show
t.SetText "W 125 mm"
t.Hide
